headline: Weekend Brief: US equities eyed for cautious Monday open as rate jitters, soft oil and big-tech overhang set tone ahead of FOMC, PCE data and mega-cap earnings
raw_text:
- US investment‑grade bond funds saw roughly $7B in outflows last week, underscoring rising rate sensitivity for financials and other credit‑exposed sectors into Monday’s open
- Oil (@CL) prices remained weak despite Middle East tanker disruptions and demand concerns, pressuring sentiment toward energy names
- Heat-driven power demand in the central US puts utilities and regional energy providers in focus at the start of the week
- Alphabet (GOOGL) and Tesla (TSLA) lost about $500B in combined market value last week on post‑earnings and AI‑spending concerns, keeping sentiment cautious around large‑cap tech
- Asian and European equity indices traded mixed to lower late last week on chip and demand worries, offering limited directional guidance for US markets
- Monday’s US macro calendar includes Durable Goods Orders, new home sales data and the Dallas Fed Manufacturing Index
- The Fed’s Monday schedule features routine publications such as the H.15 interest rate report
- Former Fed governor Kevin Warsh used weekend commentary to advocate less transparency around the Fed’s decision process, putting policy communication in focus
- Market attention is set to shift quickly to this week’s FOMC decision, PCE inflation release and earnings from Microsoft (MSFT), Meta (META), Amazon (AMZN), Apple (AAPL) and other mega‑cap tech companies
